thread.title: Dow Tumbles 190 Points as Amazon Health Plans Slam UnitedHealth

author: Ben Levisohn
title: Dow Tumbles 190 Points as Amazon Health Plans Slam UnitedHealth
text:
One of the stock market's best Januaries on record suddenly looks less good.
Illustration: iStockphoto S&P 500 futures have fallen 0.5%, while Dow Jones Industrial Average futures have dropped 190 points, or 0.7%. Nasdaq Composite futures have declined 0.5%. The S&P 500 was up 7.5% in January at Friday's close. If it closes down 0.5% today, it will be up only 6.2% this month.
If you're looking for a reason for the sudden selloff, everyone's pointing to rising bond yields. The 10-year U.S Treasury yield is trading at 2.71% this morning, and the German 5-year bund nearly closed above zero yesterday--it hasn't closed above zero since November 15, writes Deutsche Bank's Jim Reid, who sees "nothing particularly igniting the sell-off." (Remember, bond prices fall as yields rise.) Still, he's not worried. "Our US economists believe there is considerable scope for bond yields to rise before they weigh on growth and equities," Reid explains.
Rhino Trading's Michael Block goes when step further by openly mocking the bears, writing sarcastically--he makes sure to point this out--that "the great selloff of 2018 continues for a second day." Still, even if markets closed near where they are now they'd still be within a percentage point or two of their all-time highs, Block says. There's little to suggest that there's a bear market coming any time soon, as "the data and earnings and most of all, the momentum is still in the bullish camp," he continues. As if to prove his point, home prices jump 6.2% in November . "One benefit of days like yesterday is that it burns off overbought conditions, and that’s what is playing out now," Block says.
Who's buying?
Morning Movers UnitedHealth Group (UNH) has tumbled 6.3% to $232.00 after Amazon.com (AMZN), Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B) and JPMorgan Chase (JPM) announced plans to start a new company that would focus on improving employee health . CVS Health (CVS) Express Scripts (ESRX) and Humana (HUM), among others, have also dropped on the news. "We believe that this project will take years to build, and we are not changing our forward estimates at this time," Leerink's David Larsen writes in a note this morning.
Illustration: Getty Images Pfizer (PFE) has fallen 1.9% top $38.29 after reporting better-than expected earnings and meeting revenue forecasts. Pfizer also said it would earn between $2.90 a share and $3 a share in 2018, above analyst forecasts for $2.78. "The main driver of a much higher than expected 2018 EPS guidance is a tax rate that is expected to be 17%, as compared to the 23% we currently assumed in our model," writes Credit Suisse analyst Vamil Divan.
McDonald's (MCD) has declined 0.8% to $176.40 after reporting a profit of $1.71 a share on sales of $5.34 billion.. Analysts had predicted a profit of $1.59 per share on sales of $5.2 billion. Shares of McDonald's have gained 45% during the past 12 months.
Hawaiian Holdings (HA) has climbed 5.1% to $39.40 after reporting a profit of $1.10 a share on sales of $686.5 million. Analysts had predicted earnings of consensus $1.08 on revenue of $681.5 million. "Despite the favorable near-term story, we remain on the sidelines as we expect Southwest to load their Hawaii schedule and start selling and marketing tickets at a discount," Cowen's Helane Becker wrote in a note this morning.
It's a lousy day for makers of motorcycles and other recreational vehicles. Harley-Davidson (HOG) has dropped 5.8% to $52.10 as disappointing shipments trumped an earnings beat, while Polaris Industries (PII) has slumped 6.9% to $125.01 after beating revenue forecasts but "only" meeting earnings estimates . "PII shares likely trade slightly lower despite solid Q4 revs and likely conservative 2018 guidance due to (1) Q417 margin decline/2018 margin outlook, (2) ORV/snowmobile retail weakness," Wells Fargo analyst Timothy Conder wrote in a note this morning.
Danaher (DHR) has fallen 3.6% to $100 despite reporting earnings and sales that topped analyst forecasts . In reiterating his Outperform rating on the stock this morning, Cowen's Doug Schenkel might have struck on the reason: "We acknowledge that Danaher stock has had a strong run over the past few months and now trades at healthy multiples," he writes.
United Continental Holdings (UAL) has gained 1.6% to $66.85 after getting upgraded to Overweight from Underweight at JPMorgan.
MetLife Messes Up MetLife (MET) was supposed to report earnings on Wednesday. Not quite.
Illustration: Getty Images After yesterday's closer, MetLife warned that it would increase its pension reserves by $525 million to $575 million due to an accounting mistake. As a result, MetLife said it would postpone its quarterly earnings report, which was scheduled for Jan.31. As a result, shares of MetLife have dropped 7% to $50.61 this morning.
Should investors be panicking? B.Riley FBR's Randy Binner doesn't think so. He's no fan of the stock--he cut it to Neutral in October 2017--but he doesn't believe the charge says anything about MetLife's reserves overall. It also helps that interest rates are rising, which generally helps insurance reserves. "This appears to be an isolated and relatively small matter," Binner writes.
Even if the market doesn't quite think so?
The View From Silicon Valley Consider this a tale of two realities.
Illustration: Getty Images Augmented reality, an understudy to virtual reality after years of unfulfilled promise, is ready to take the leading role in mixed reality.
Advances in mobile technology, and the popularity of smart glasses, have thrust AR into the mainstream. By the end of 2022, according to market researcher Digi-Capital, AR will boast an installed base of 3.5 billion devices, and revenue of $85 billion to $90 billion. VR, by comparison, will be installed on 50 million to 60 million devices, creating $10 billion to $15 billion.
AR is benefitting from its ubiquity on popular computing platforms such as Apple’s (AAPL) ARKit, Alphabet's (GOOGL) ARCore, Facebook’s (FB) Camera Effects and Snap’s (SNAP) Lens Studio.
Far from dormant, VR will be visible in the form of Samsung Gear VR, Google Daydream View and Facebook’s Oculus Go for entertainment and some enterprise use. But there is little doubt that phone makers and developers are shifting their focus more towards mobile AR, says Tim Merel, managing director of Digi-Capital.
The biggest opportunities for AR could come in e-commerce sales and corporate training. If and when Apple launches smartphone-tethered smart glasses, hardware sales could become AR’s second largest revenue stream, according to Digi-Capital.
The massive installed base for mobile AR could especially be a boon for Facebook ( Messenger , WhatsApp , Instagram ), Snap ( Snapchat , Bitmoji ), Tencent ( WeChat , QQ ) and other social/messaging platforms.
“AR/VR is the fourth wave of consumer technology, and AR could be bigger,” Merel says. “We’re still only at the start of what that wave could become.” -- Jon Swartz
